First, there's really no such thing as an ad hominem "attack." An ad hominem is a logical fallacy - specifically the fallacy of addressing the person presenting an argument rather than the argument being presented.

And an "assessment of credibility" is in fact an ad hominem. It's just a more polite one, and a more seductive one.

An argument is either valid or it's not. While it's at least possible that a (necessarily subjective and likely biased) assessment of "credibility" might provide some indication of the likelihood of the validity of an argument, it proves absolutely nothing. It, in fact, doesn't even address the actual argument that's been presented at all. That's why it's a fallacy.

Ad hominem is a fallacy which tries to dismiss an argument based on attacking the speaker (whether accurately or not) without addressing the points made.

Assessing credibility, if done in reference to an argument, is ad hominem (You are a liar so I dismiss your point without reasoning). That's because assessing arguments is the wrong time to assess credibility. Credibility assessment is how you decide whether or not you trust someone to be providing accurate facts, which are distinct from reasoning or argument. Using credibility assessment non-fallaciously would be saying "I don't trust you, so give me a credible source to back up that statistic."

If the facts are universally agreed on, credibility assessment is irrelevant and a form of ad hominem. If they aren't, then chances are that credibility is where the argument is happening and assessing credibility is the most important thing for both parties to be doing.
